literal: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part Two
idiomatic: Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 2)

literal: Biographies 6: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part Two
idiomatic: Biographies 6 — Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 2)

literal: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Heping.
idiomatic: Yun, Prince of Rencheng, received his fief in the fifth year of Heping.

literal: As a youth he was clever; at five, when Jingmu died, he wept without cease.
idiomatic: Clever even as a boy, at five when Jingmu died he wept without stopping.

literal: Taiwu took him in his arms and wept, saying: "How can you know enough to have the mind of a grown man!
idiomatic: Taiwu took him in his arms and wept. "How is it you already have a grown man's heart?

literal: " Under Xianwen he was made commander of all military affairs within and without the court and Director of the Inner Palace at the Center, heard civil suits, and won great praise of the age.
idiomatic: Under Xianwen he commanded all armies at court and in the field, directed the Inner Palace at the Center, heard civil suits, and won wide renown.

literal: When Xianwen wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao, kings, dukes, and grandees dared speak first of none.
idiomatic: When Xianwen wished to abdicate to Zitui, Prince of Jingzhao, none among kings, dukes, and grandees dared speak first.

literal: Yun advanced and said: "Father passing the throne to son has long been the way; since Imperial Wei rose there has been no change.
idiomatic: Yun stepped forward. "Father passing rule to son is an ancient way; since Imperial Wei rose, that line has never been broken.

literal: " Grand Commandant Yuan He also advanced and said it could not be done, and begged deep thought for the Prince of Rencheng's words.
idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan He added that it could not be done and begged the throne to heed the Prince of Rencheng.

literal: Yuan Pi of Dongyang and others advanced and said: "The crown prince's sagely virtue was long manifest, yet in truth he is still very young.
idiomatic: Yuan Pi of Dongyang and others said, "The crown prince's virtue is plain, yet he is still a child.

literal: Your Majesty wishes to exalt solitary goodness—what of the ancestral temples?
idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks private ease—what becomes of the ancestral temples?

literal: The emperor said: "The heir's palace is orthodox; the lords assist him—what cannot be done?
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The heir holds the orthodox line; the lords will assist him—what could be impossible?

literal: " Thereupon the throne passed to Emperor Xiaowen.
idiomatic: Thereupon the throne passed to Emperor Xiaowen.

literal: Later, when the Rouran raided the frontier, Yun was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and followed Xianwen to campaign.
idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier Yun was made Grand Commander of the Center Army and followed Xianwen to war.

literal: Crossing the Great Marsh, Yun said: "The barbarians' horses have never seen the Wu-head shield; if this shield is placed in front, breaking them is certain.
idiomatic: Crossing the Great Marsh, Yun said, "Their horses have never seen the Wu-head shield; put it in front and we are sure to break them.

literal: " The emperor followed this, ordered the Tiele chiefs, and grasped their hands in labor and send-off.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed, ordered the Tiele chiefs, and took their hands in farewell.

literal: Thereupon they sang in succession and drove forward in formation.
idiomatic: They sang as one and drove forward in formation.

literal: A great defeat was inflicted and their chieftains were captured.
idiomatic: The army won a great victory and took their chieftains.

literal: Later the Di of Chouchi rebelled; Yun was again ordered to campaign and pacify them.
idiomatic: When the Chouchi Di rebelled he was again sent to campaign and pacify them.

literal: He was removed and made commander with an open office and Inspector of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was then given an open office and made inspector of Xuzhou.

literal: When Yun's grand consort Lady Gai died, he memorialized asking to resign his post.
idiomatic: When his grand consort Lady Gai died, Yun asked to resign his post.

literal: Xianwen did not permit it.
idiomatic: Xianwen refused.

literal: Yun wailed until illness struck; only then was he allowed.
idiomatic: Yun wailed until he fell ill; only then was he released.

literal: By nature he was good at comforting men; he won the hearts of Xu deeply, and the people clung to him, sending gifts of money and goods—all of which he refused.
idiomatic: He was skilled at winning men and deeply won Xu; the people clung to him and sent money and goods, but he accepted none.

literal: Transferred again to Inspector of Jizhou, he won the lower ranks' hearts exceedingly.
idiomatic: Made inspector of Jizhou, he won the common people's hearts even more.

literal: Thereupon the whole province asked each household to submit five feet of silk and five sheng of grain to repay Yun's grace.
idiomatic: The whole province then asked each household to give five feet of silk and five sheng of grain in thanks for Yun's grace.

literal: Xiaowen praised this and issued an edict proclaimed throughout the realm to show encouragement.
idiomatic: Xiaowen praised it and proclaimed an edict through the realm as encouragement.

literal: He was transferred to Grand General of Chang'an Garrison and Inspector of Yongzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to grand general of Chang'an Garrison and inspector of Yongzhou.

literal: Yun cultivated himself with integrity and care, attended to common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and robbery ceased; more than a thousand in the province praised him.
idiomatic: Yun lived with integrity, minded common lawsuits, checked the powerful, and robbery ceased; more than a thousand in the province praised him.

literal: In the fifth year of Taihe he died in the province; he left orders for a plain burial and no funeral gifts; his sons all followed his will.
idiomatic: In Taihe year 5 he died in the province, ordering a plain burial and no funeral gifts; his sons obeyed.

literal: Posthumous title Kang; buried with honor at Jinling in Yunzhong.
idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Kang and buried with honor at Jinling in Yunzhong.

literal: His eldest son Cheng, styled Daojing, loved learning from youth, had fine hair and beard, graceful bearing, clear and eloquent speech, a voice like a suspended bell.
idiomatic: His eldest son Cheng, styled Daojing, loved learning from youth, had fine hair and beard, graceful bearing, and a clear, bell-like voice.

literal: When Prince Kang died, his mourning was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: When Prince Kang died, his mourning was famed for filial piety.

literal: He inherited the title and was further made Grand General Who Pacifies the North.
idiomatic: He inherited the title and was further made Grand General Who Pacifies the North.

literal: Because the Di and Qiang rebelled, he was made Grand General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: When the Di and Qiang rebelled he was made Grand General Who Conquers the South and inspector of Liangzhou.

literal: Empress Dowager Wenming received him and admonished him, turning to Director of the Secretariat Li Chong and saying: "This boy's spirit shines forth; he will be a leader among the imperial kin. On this mission he will not disgrace his charge—I do not speak idly.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming received and warned him, then told Director of the Secretariat Li Chong, "This boy's spirit shines; he will lead the imperial kin. He will not disgrace this mission—I do not speak idly.

literal: " At the province he guided and won attachment; the southwest submitted in good faith.
idiomatic: At the province he guided and won men; the southwest submitted in good faith.

literal: He was added Palace Attendant, granted one suit of robes and one yellow horse, to mark his ability.
idiomatic: He was made palace attendant, granted a suit of robes and a yellow horse, to mark his ability.

literal: Transferred to commander with an open office and Inspector of Xuzhou, he won great fame and achievement.
idiomatic: Made commander with an open office and inspector of Xuzhou, he won great fame and achievement.

literal: Coming to the capital he was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
idiomatic: At the capital he was received in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

literal: Xiaowen said to Cheng: "Long ago Zichan of Zheng cast the penal code and Shu Xiang of Jin opposed it.
idiomatic: Xiaowen said to Cheng, "Long ago Zichan of Zheng cast the penal code and Shu Xiang of Jin opposed it.

literal: Both were worthy men—who in the end was right?
idiomatic: Both were worthy—who was right in the end?

literal: He replied: "Zheng was few and weak, subject to a strong neighbor; the people's going and staying could not be governed without penal law, so he cast the code to show authority.
idiomatic: He replied, "Zheng was few and weak, subject to a strong neighbor; the people's going and staying needed penal law, so he cast the code to show authority.

literal: Though it departed from ancient form, it fit the expedient of the age.
idiomatic: Though it departed from antiquity, it fit the age's expedient.

literal: The emperor was then reforming institutions and deeply approved his answer, smiling: "Prince of Rencheng wishes to be Wei's Zichan.
idiomatic: The emperor was reforming institutions and deeply approved, smiling, "Prince of Rencheng would be Wei's Zichan.

literal: I am now creating new court institutions and shall share ten-thousand-year achievement with Prince of Rencheng.
idiomatic: I am now creating new court institutions and shall share enduring achievement with Prince of Rencheng.

literal: Later he was summoned as Director of the Secretariat and changed to Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later he was summoned as director of the Secretariat and then director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Qi's Yu Bi came to court; seeing Cheng's voice resonant and elegant, his bearing refined, he told Chief of Guests Zhang Yi: "Formerly Wei's Prince of Rencheng was famed for martial prowess; now Wei's Prince of Rencheng is praised for letters."
idiomatic: Yu Bi of Qi came to court; seeing Cheng's resonant voice and refined bearing, he told Chief of Guests Zhang Yi, "Once Wei's Prince of Rencheng was famed for war; now he is praised for letters."

literal: At that time an edict extended the four temples' sons down to great-great-grandsons' descendants and held a clan feast in the Hall of Imperial Trust.
idiomatic: An edict then gathered sons of the four temples down to great-great-grandsons for a clan feast in the Hall of Imperial Trust.

literal: They were not ranked by title but all ordered by zhao and mu sequence, using family rites.
idiomatic: They were not ranked by title but ordered by zhao and mu, with family rites.

literal: The emperor said: "The rites are finished; I wish each of the clan to speak his heart—compose poems as you will.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The rites are done; let each of the clan speak his heart—compose poems as you will.

literal: He specially ordered Cheng to make linked seven-character rhyme; he and Xiaowen wagered back and forth until utmost joy, and only at night did they stop.
idiomatic: He ordered Cheng to make linked seven-character rhyme; he and Xiaowen wagered until joy peaked and night ended the feast.

literal: Later the emperor outwardly showed a southern campaign but inwardly meant to plan the move, with Qi at the left bay of the Bright Hall.
idiomatic: Later he outwardly showed a southern campaign but meant to plan the move, with Qi at the Bright Hall's left bay.

literal: He ordered Grand Master of Rites Wang Chen in person to divine by tortoise and yarrow the matter of campaigning south; the omen met Hexagram Ge.
idiomatic: He ordered Grand Master of Rites Wang Chen to divine by tortoise and yarrow a southern campaign; the omen was Ge.

literal: Cheng advanced and said: "The Changes says Ge means change—it will change the mandate between ruler and subject; Tang and Wu obtained it as auspicious.
idiomatic: Cheng advanced. "The Changes says Ge means change—it would change the mandate between ruler and subject; Tang and Wu found that auspicious.

literal: Your Majesty already holds all under heaven; to divine a campaign today cannot be called revolution in full—this cannot be wholly auspicious.
idiomatic: Your Majesty already holds the realm; to divine a campaign today cannot be wholly revolution—this cannot be wholly auspicious.

literal: The emperor said sternly: "This image says the great man changes by force—how is it not auspicious!
idiomatic: The emperor said sternly, "This image says the great man changes by force—how is it not auspicious?

literal: The carriage returned to the palace and Cheng was summoned; before he mounted the steps the emperor called from afar: "The Ge just now—I wish to discuss it again.
idiomatic: The carriage returned and Cheng was summoned; before he mounted the steps Xiaowen called, "That Ge just now—I wish to discuss it again.

literal: My anger at the Bright Hall was fear that the crowd would all speak and thwart my great plan, so I showed a stern face to frighten civil and military alike.
idiomatic: My anger at the Bright Hall was fear the crowd would thwart my great plan, so I showed a stern face to frighten court and army.

literal: Then he spoke to Cheng alone: "The state rose from the northern land and dwelt at Pingcheng; though rich in the four seas, culture and the cart-track were not one.
idiomatic: Then he spoke to Cheng alone. "The state rose in the north and dwelt at Pingcheng; though it held the four seas, culture and the cart-track were not one.

literal: This region is a field for military use—not where civilization is raised.
idiomatic: This is a field for war—not where civilization is raised.

literal: The imperial seat lies between Xiao and Han; the royal capital is in He and Luo—by this great move to glorify the central plain, what does Prince of Rencheng think?
idiomatic: Between Xiao and Han lies the imperial seat; He and Luo are the royal capital—by this great move to glorify the central plain, what does Prince of Rencheng think?

literal: Cheng deeply approved the matter.
idiomatic: Cheng deeply approved.

literal: The emperor said: "Prince of Rencheng is my Zifang.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Prince of Rencheng is my Zifang.

literal: He was added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and Junior Tutor of the Heir, and also concurrently Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was added Grand General Who Pacifies the Army and junior tutor of the heir, and also left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When the carriage reached Luoyang and settled the plan to move the capital, Cheng was ordered to ride post-horses north and ask the hundred offices there, debating what could or could not be done.
idiomatic: When the carriage reached Luoyang and settled the capital move, Cheng was ordered to ride post north and ask the hundred offices whether it could be done.

literal: He said: "We lately discussed Ge; now this is truly what is called Ge.
idiomatic: He said, "We lately discussed Ge; now this is truly Ge.

literal: When Cheng reached the northern capital, all who heard the move edict were startled.
idiomatic: At the northern capital all who heard the move edict were startled.

literal: Cheng cited present and past and slowly enlightened them; the crowd then opened and submitted.
idiomatic: Cheng cited present and past and slowly enlightened them; the crowd then submitted.

literal: He galloped south to report and met the carriage at Huatai.
idiomatic: He galloped south to report and met the carriage at Huatai.

literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "Had it not been for Prince of Rencheng, my undertaking would not have been achieved.
idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased. "Without Prince of Rencheng my undertaking would not have been achieved.

literal: He followed in attendance at the Ye palace.
idiomatic: He followed in attendance at the Ye palace.

literal: He was made Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: He was made director of the Ministry of Personnel.

literal: When the carriage toured north from the northern capital, Cheng was left to grade the old officials.
idiomatic: When the carriage toured north from the northern capital, Cheng was left to grade the old officials.

literal: At first, from dukes and marquises down, Wei had tens of thousands idle and scattered without duties.
idiomatic: At first, from dukes and marquises down, tens of thousands in Wei were idle and without duties.

literal: Cheng graded them in three ranks, measured excellence and defect, and used each to the limit of ability—none bore resentment.
idiomatic: Cheng graded them in three ranks, measured each by ability, and used all without resentment.

literal: When the carriage returned to Luoyang he again held the right vice directorship concurrently.
idiomatic: When the carriage returned to Luoyang he again held the right vice directorship.

literal: The emperor reached North Mang and then visited Hong Pool, ordering Cheng to attend aboard the dragon boat.
idiomatic: The emperor reached North Mang and visited Hong Pool, ordering Cheng to attend aboard the dragon boat.

literal: The emperor said: "Last night I dreamed an old man bowing by the road, saying he was Jin's Palace Attendant Ji Shao—therefore he came to meet me; my spirit was low and fearful, as though he had a request.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Last night I dreamed an old man bowing by the road, saying he was Jin's Palace Attendant Ji Shao come to meet me; my spirit was low and fearful, as though he had a request.

literal: Cheng said: "Your Majesty passed Yin's ruins and mourned Bi Gan, reached Luoyang and met Ji Shao in dream—this must be longing for grace that moved the dream.
idiomatic: Cheng said, "Your Majesty mourned Bi Gan at Yin's ruins and met Ji Shao at Luoyang in dream—longing for grace must have moved the dream.

literal: The emperor said: "Since I had this dream, perhaps it is as Prince of Rencheng said.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since I had this dream, perhaps it is as Prince of Rencheng said.

literal: Thereupon his tomb domain was sought and envoys sent to mourn and sacrifice.
idiomatic: His tomb domain was sought and envoys sent to mourn and sacrifice.

literal: After Qi's Emperor Ming had deposed and murdered his lord to establish himself, Qi's Inspector of Yongzhou Cao Wu asked to bring Xiangyang within.
idiomatic: After Qi's Emperor Ming deposed and murdered his lord, Cao Wu, inspector of Yongzhou, asked to bring Xiangyang within.

literal: The carriage was about to go in person; Cheng and Prince of Xianyang Xi, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, Director of the Secretariat Feng Yan, Minister of Works Mu Liang, and Grand General Who Guards the South Li Chong were summoned to deliberate.
idiomatic: The carriage was about to go in person; Cheng, Prince of Xianyang Xi, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, Director of the Secretariat Feng Yan, Minister of Works Mu Liang, and Grand General Who Guards the South Li Chong were summoned to deliberate.

literal: Xi and the rest said some that one should go, some that one should stop.
idiomatic: Some said go, some said stop.

literal: The emperor said: "The crowd's views differ; there should be guest and host to stir each other.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Views differ; let guest and host stir each other.

literal: Prince of Rencheng and Grand General Who Guards the South argue to stay; I shall argue to go.
idiomatic: Prince of Rencheng and Li Chong argue to stay; I shall argue to go.

literal: You all sit and listen; the elder side prevails.
idiomatic: You all sit and listen; the elder side prevails.

literal: Thereupon the emperor went back and forth several rounds; the carriage then marched south, not following Cheng and Li Chong's words.
idiomatic: The emperor debated back and forth; the carriage then marched south, not following Cheng and Li Chong.

literal: Later, following the campaign to Xianhu, he returned to the capital because illness grew severe.
idiomatic: Later, on campaign at Xianhu, severe illness made him return to the capital.

literal: When the carriage returned to Luo, kings, dukes, and attendant ministers were received at the Clear Splendor Hall.
idiomatic: When the carriage returned to Luo, kings, dukes, and ministers were received at the Clear Splendor Hall.

literal: The emperor said: "Since this hall was completed I have not held feast and music with kings and dukes.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Since this hall was finished I have not feasted with kings and dukes.

literal: Today with you worthies I wish none high not to ascend, none small not to enter.
idiomatic: Today with you worthies I wish none too high to ascend, none too small to enter.

literal: Thereupon they followed the Transforming Flow channel.
idiomatic: They followed the Transforming Flow channel.

literal: The emperor said: "This winding water takes the meaning of Qian's way curving to completion—ten thousand things without stagnation.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "This winding water takes Qian's way curving to completion—ten thousand things without stagnation.

literal: Next they reached the Wash-Weariness Pool.
idiomatic: Next they reached the Wash-Weariness Pool.

literal: The emperor said: "This pool also has fine fish.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "This pool also has fine fish.

literal: Cheng said: "As the ode says, 'Fish there in the weeds, with heads well shown.
idiomatic: Cheng said, "As the ode says, 'Fish there in the weeds, with heads well shown.'

literal: The emperor said: "Then take 'The king is at the Spirit Marsh; how the fish leap in multitudes.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then take 'The king is at the Spirit Marsh; how the fish leap in multitudes.'

literal: Next they reached the View-Virtue Hall.
idiomatic: Next they reached the View-Virtue Hall.
